focus.title: 欧盟碳边境调节机制过渡期收官在即，中国出口企业须加速碳数据合规布局
focus.summary: 欧盟CBAM过渡期将于2026年底结束，2027年起进入正式征税阶段。中国钢铁、铝、化肥等行业出口企业面临碳排放数据申报与核查的紧迫要求。企业需尽快建立产品级碳足迹核算体系，完善与欧盟进口商的數據对接，并关注间接排放核算规则的细化。未合规申报可能导致贸易受阻或成本激增，建议企业提前开展碳管理审计并探索低碳生产路径。
focus.source: 来源：欧盟委员会气候行动总司 · 2026.11.18
focus.title_en: EU CBAM Transitional Period Nears End: Chinese Exporters Urged to Accelerate Carbon Data Compliance
focus.summary_en: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) transitional phase concludes at the end of 2026, with definitive taxation starting in 2027. Chinese exporters in steel, aluminum, and fertilizers face urgent requirements for carbon emission data reporting and verification. Companies should establish product-level carbon footprint accounting systems, enhance data interfaces with EU importers, and monitor refined rules on indirect emissions. Non-compliance may lead to trade disruptions or cost surges; early carbon management audits and low-carbon production pathways are recommended.

case.title: 新加坡仲裁庭认定跨境电商合同中的电子签名有效，中方卖家获赔违约金
case.summary: 某中国跨境电商卖家与新加坡买方通过电子邮件订立供货合同，买方违约后以电子签名不符合《新加坡电子交易法》为由抗辩。仲裁庭认为，双方往来邮件及可验证的电子签名满足法定要求，合同成立有效，裁决买方支付违约金。本案提示出海企业：在普通法域，电子合同效力通常得到承认，但需确保签名可归属、意图明确且记录完整，建议在合同中明确约定电子通信的约束力。
case.source: 来源：新加坡国际仲裁中心典型案例摘要 · 2026.11
case.title_en: Singapore Tribunal Upholds E-Signature in Cross-Border E-Commerce Contract, Chinese Seller Awarded Damages
case.summary_en: A Chinese cross-border e-commerce seller concluded a supply contract with a Singaporean buyer via email. When the buyer defaulted, it argued that the electronic signatures did not comply with Singapore's Electronic Transactions Act. The tribunal held that the exchanged emails and verifiable e-signatures satisfied statutory requirements, rendering the contract valid and enforceable, and ordered the buyer to pay liquidated damages. The case reminds outbound businesses that electronic contracts are generally recognized in common law jurisdictions, but signatures must be attributable, intent clear, and records complete. Explicit clauses on the binding force of electronic communications are advisable.

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区跨境数据流动新规落地，企业需关注“数据出境安全评估”与“标准合同”双轨制
policy.summary: 粤港澳大湾区近日发布跨境数据流动便利化措施，进一步明确数据出境安全评估、个人信息出境标准合同及认证三条路径的适用条件。对于年出境个人信息超过一定数量的企业，须申报安全评估；未达门槛的可选择标准合同或认证。新政强调“一事一议”的便利化通道，但企业仍需完成数据分类分级、开展个人信息保护影响评估，并留存记录。建议跨境业务企业梳理数据资产，选择合规路径。
policy.source: 来源：广东省政务服务数据管理局 · 2026.11
policy.title_en: New Cross-Border Data Flow Rules in Greater Bay Area: Dual Track of Security Assessment and Standard Contracts
policy.summary_en: The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area has issued facilitation measures for cross-border data flows, clarifying the applicable conditions for three paths: security assessment, standard contracts for personal information export, and certification. Companies exporting personal information above a certain annual threshold must file for security assessment; those below may choose standard contracts or certification. The new policy emphasizes a case-by-case facilitation channel, but enterprises still need to complete data classification and grading, conduct personal information protection impact assessments, and maintain records. Cross-border businesses should map data assets and select a compliant path.
policy.source_en: Source: Guangdong Provincial Government Services and Data Administration · 2026.11

analysis.title: 秦林蒿律师研判：美国对外投资审查新规扩围，科技企业须重构跨境投资合规架构
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师研判：美国近期拟扩大对外投资审查范围，将更多涉及半导体、人工智能和量子技术的交易纳入申报要求。中国科技企业通过境外子公司或基金进行的对美投资可能触发审查，甚至面临强制剥离风险。建议企业：一是在交易前进行筛查，确认是否涉及“受关注国家”及敏感技术；二是设计多层交易架构时，避免规避意图；三是完善内部合规流程，对现有投资进行复盘。同时，应关注中国反制法规下的申报义务，实现双向合规。
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin's view: Expanded US Outbound Investment Review Requires Tech Firms to Restructure Cross-Border Compliance
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's view: The US is poised to expand its outbound investment review to cover more transactions involving semiconductors, AI, and quantum technologies. Chinese tech companies investing in the US through offshore subsidiaries or funds may trigger reviews and even face divestment risks. Recommendations: first, screen transactions to identify 'countries of concern' and sensitive technologies; second, avoid circumvention intent when designing multi-layer structures; third, strengthen internal compliance and review existing investments. Companies should also monitor filing obligations under China's countermeasures to achieve dual compliance.
